scenes.headline: How OpenAI claims to pin the matrix exponent at 9/4
scenes.sub: What is proved, what Lean checks, and what is still a claim
scenes.say: I'm Ninebark. How fast can two n by n matrices be multiplied? OpenAI now says: n to the nine fourths, and no faster.

heads: Strassen, then Schönhage, then Coppersmith and Winograd
24 November: the floor rises to meet it
params.lowerLabel: lower bound: the answer has n² entries

steps.say: Strassen used seven products where the schoolbook uses eight. Recursion gave two point eight oh seven, and by nineteen ninety the bound was two point three seven five.
Then thirty-six years of work on one tensor moved it by less than a hundredth.
In October, OpenAI's paper dropped it to nine fourths. Six groups of human authors have reproved that since.
The lower bound never left two. The new paper claims it rises all the way to nine fourths.

left.title: From above
items: six human papers since, one constructive
left.say: The upper bound is settled. Six independent write-ups, one of them an explicit algorithm.

right.title: From below
items: at least n^(9/4)/2 gates, every n
right.say: The lower bound is one long preprint, and nobody outside OpenAI has explained it yet.

scenes.credit: The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths, Figure 1

steps.say: The proof starts from a picture. Three factors at three sites, and each index is a wire between two of them.
A rank decomposition replaces the wires with one label that all three share.

parts.note: three wire lengths, one per index
parts.say: Give every wire a length. The tensor costs the perimeter.
In flat space the shared label costs half the perimeter, and the bound is two. On a tripod it is nine fourths.

scenes.credit: The matrix multiplication exponent is nine fourths, Figure 2

steps.say: If matrices multiplied faster than nine fourths, the paper shows tensor networks could be compressed again and again.
Then checking lists for repeated entries would get too cheap, which a counting bound forbids.

scenes.title: What Lean checks

items.text: Not the gate count per size

scenes.say: The exact exponent is stated against plain Mathlib and proved with standard axioms, and one outside builder reproduced it. The per-size gate count is not in Lean.

scenes.text: The top is settled. The floor is machine-checked. Nobody outside OpenAI has explained why yet.
scenes.say: The top is settled. The floor is machine-checked. Nobody outside OpenAI has explained why yet.
Nine fourths from above, nine fourths from below, and a proof still waiting for a human reader.
